statement: Every positive homotopy group of the relative one-partition quotient-kernel subgroup is zero. This subgroup lies in the original plane operator centralizer, fixes the exterior of an invariant union of one-partition open orbits, and preserves each orbit and every actual global quotient map. Every based sphere family contracts globally with jointly continuous inverse and pointwise control by the entire compact family. For a loop the stronger forward and inverse prefix-track inclusions hold. This gives arbitrary frontier and orbit-accumulation control without quotient compactness or a separate ambient-null assumption.
depends_on: C32 exact two-point winding comparison and ambient-null restriction theorem; C43-C44 actual source and target covering maps; C45 dependent real quotient comparison; C48 complete proper-operator affine fiber normal forms and inverse bracketing; C53 full global quotient family
manuscript_passages: Section 23, folios 140-141, scans 279-281; Part C(b), infinite-operator zero-level comparison and relative one-partition frontier extension
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The fiber interpolation is in the proved actual operator-normalized coordinates, commutes with every original deck map, and is compared after projection to the original global loop by exact pointwise prefix-track inclusions.
notes: A nonempty one-partition family supplies a nontrivial nonopen target orbit outside the chosen union. A relative loop fixes two distinct points there, so the exact plane two-point winding is zero and C32 closes every based source-cover lift. For higher spheres the covering lift instead exists directly on the simply connected product of the universal source cover with the parameter sphere; lifting inverse families proves the actual inverse identities. Connectedness kills all operator and target deck increments. Quotient-kernel equations make the real base coordinate fixed. Convex interpolation of the increasing fiber map preserves every affine operator equation, including orientation reversals, and every source deck equation. Each interpolated point lies in its compact sphere-family orbit, using any parameter path from the basepoint; inverse bracketing gives the inverse-family inclusion. For loops these inclusions use the original prefixes. Compactness then proves all frontier and mixed-orbit limits uniformly, independent of chart choices. Operator-stabilizer commutation makes transported choices well defined. The resulting based homotopies give disk fillings in every positive degree. No contractibility of the whole group or existence of a lift of a nontrivial quotient deformation is asserted; that lifting/decomposition problem remains open in C12.
